name: Warm low-poly dusk
one_line: Chunky faceted hills, one lit window, the last of the sun.
look_words: A small faceted world at the end of the day. Olive and moss greens for the ground, terracotta and warm stone for rocks and walls, long violet shadows, a peach horizon under a deep blue sky. Shapes are chunky and flat-shaded, two tones per surface, no texture noise. One low warm sun does the work; amber is kept for lit windows, lanterns and the things to collect. Motion is slow: smoke, a swaying tree, drifting dust. Materials are matte, like painted wood and clay. Avoid glossy surfaces, bloom, neon, pure black and busy textures.

palette.name: warm dusk
palette.notes: Amber is the reward colour (windows, lanterns, pickups); bright aqua is for the goal or water you can use. Red only for harm. The player is the palest warm thing on screen.

look_wish: flat shading with a soft outline, or none

upgrade.why: one sun-tinted air for the whole world, so far hills fade into the dusk sky

music.mood: slow, warm, plucked strings and a soft pad
music.notes: Leave room for crickets and wind.

sound_feel: soft, wooden, close; footsteps on dirt, a distant bell

frames.prompt: Low-poly island at dusk seen from a third-person camera behind a small traveller with a red scarf walking a dirt path toward a stone cottage with one lit window. Chunky faceted hills in olive green, two tones per surface, terracotta rocks, a few round trees, long soft violet shadows, peach horizon under a deep blue sky, a little haze. Warm, calm, lived-in. Flat-shaded polygons, no texture noise. Gameplay view of a stylised indie video game, no text, no user interface, no logos, no watermark.

Low-poly fishing dock at dusk, high three-quarter camera. A small figure with a red scarf stands at the end of a wooden pier holding a lantern, a little boat tied beside it, olive-green faceted hills and terracotta cliffs behind, a few glowing amber windows in a hut. Long violet shadows, peach and rose horizon, deep blue sky, calm flat water. Chunky flat-shaded polygons, two tones per surface.
